title: Sample 19-2: Linear Key Format

illustrates.quote: Linear Key Format. When letters are printed above or below the line(s) of code characters: a. To ensure the code will be read as individual letters, insert the grade 1 passage indicator... b. Use the next two consecutive braille lines (margins 1-1) for the code characters.

blocks.text: Assign a symbol or number for each letter of the alphabet.
blocks.features: Given braille (lines 1-4) shows a uniform indent on every line — built blocked:true.

blocks.text: Share the code with anyone who will read or return a response to your written message.
Here is a secret code you can use.
The puzzle code symbols are under the letters.

a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z
2  4  6  8  1  3  5  7  9  10 /  *  &  z  _  ]  (  7  8  9  0  ...
blocks.features: A 26-letter linear key: the alphabet on one braille line (margins 1-1, per 19.2.2b), the corresponding devised code character/number directly below each letter on the next line, per 19.2.2d. Enclosed in a ruled box and one grade-1 passage (dot locator + capitals passage indicator, source line 9: '""=;;;,,,'). Emboss has no column-alignment mechanism to place a code character directly under its own letter (F-219), no dot-locator emission (F-220), and no box mechanism reused for this content.

print.notes: An introductory paragraph, a short lead-in sentence, a transcriber's note explaining the format, and the letter/code linear key table itself.
print.printFeatures: Paragraph, then a 26-column two-row key table pairing each alphabet letter with a devised code symbol/number.
